issues.description: The template class GroverTwoQubitWithoutAuxiliaryQubit defines an __init__ that accepts a parameter (num_qubits: int) while the reference solution's __init__ has no parameters. This mismatch in constructor signatures can confuse students about how to instantiate the class and whether they must provide a num_qubits argument when following the exercise instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent. Either remove the unused num_qubits parameter from the template __init__ (so both template and solution use a parameterless constructor), or update the solution to accept num_qubits and use it to set up the circuit. Preferably update the template to match the solution (no parameter) and adjust the problem text to describe how many qubits will be used.

issues.description: The template's simulate method for the two-qubit Grover exercise is annotated to return list[complex], but the solution implementation returns a Qiskit statevector object (result.get_statevector / Statevector). The problem text asks for 'return the statevector', but the template's type hint does not match the concrete type used in the solution, which may confuse students about the expected return object/type.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the type annotation and documentation. Either update the template method's return annotation to a Qiskit-compatible type (e.g. Statevector or numpy.ndarray) and mention that a Statevector is acceptable, or change the solution to return a plain list[complex] (e.g. statevector.data.tolist()). Prefer updating the template and problem text to reference Qiskit's Statevector (from qiskit.quantum_info) for clarity.
